summary: The Reach Oxford Scholarship pays course fees, a living grant and one return flight a year for undergraduates from low-income (OECD DAC-list) countries, including Nigeria, who cannot study in their own country for political or financial reasons. Only about 2–3 awards are made each year, so it goes to applicants with the highest academic ability, real financial need and strong social commitment. You must first apply to Oxford through UCAS (deadline 15 October 2026 for 2027 entry), then complete a separate scholarship form by 26 January 2027.
lookfor: Highest academic ability (you must win an Oxford place first)
Financial need: you cannot fund Oxford yourself
Inability to study in your own country (political or financial reasons)
Social commitment and intention to return home after study
Priority to students seeking their first degree
cycle: 2027 entry: UCAS application by 6pm UK time, 15 October 2026; admissions tests in October 2026; written work by 10 November; online interviews early to mid-December 2026; admissions decisions 12 January 2027; Reach Oxford form opens January 2027 and closes 26 January 2027; scholarship selection April 2027; results end of May 2027.

eligibility.q: Are you a national of a country on the OECD DAC list (Nigeria and most African countries are included)?
eligibility.no: Reach Oxford is not open to you; look at other Oxford undergraduate funding or home-country scholarships.

eligibility.q: Are you applying for a first undergraduate degree at Oxford in a subject other than Medicine?
eligibility.no: Medicine is excluded. Graduates should look at Clarendon, Rhodes or Weidenfeld-Hoffmann for postgraduate study.

eligibility.q: Do you hold (or will you hold) qualifications Oxford accepts — e.g. A-levels, International A-levels or the IB? (WASSCE/WAEC alone is not accepted.)
eligibility.no: Take A-levels, International A-levels or the IB first, then apply in a later year.

eligibility.q: Can you show you cannot afford Oxford and cannot study in your own country for political or financial reasons?
eligibility.no: Reach Oxford is need-based. If you can fund your studies, apply to Oxford without it.

eligibility.q: Do you intend to return to your home country after your degree?
eligibility.no: Return is expected for this award.

steps.title: Check you can apply to Oxford at all
steps.why: Reach Oxford only considers people who apply for an Oxford place. Oxford does not accept WASSCE alone for undergraduate entry.
do: Open Oxford's 'International qualifications' page and find your country.
Confirm you have or will have an accepted qualification (A-levels, International A-levels, IB).
Open the Reach Oxford page and check your country is on the eligible list.
Note: if you have not already submitted UCAS for 2027 entry by 15 October 2026, plan for 2028 entry instead.
tips: Many Nigerian applicants take Cambridge International A-levels at a private school or study centre for this reason.
avoid: Applying with WAEC/NECO results only — the application will not be competitive.
check: I have, or am taking, an Oxford-accepted qualification.

steps.title: Understand how Reach Oxford is decided
steps.why: With only 2–3 awards, you need top academics plus clear financial need and social commitment.
do: Read the Reach Oxford page fully: eligibility, cover, dates.
Write a short note on why you cannot study in your own country (financial or political reasons) — be honest and specific.
List your community service or social commitment examples.
List backup options (e.g. other UK or US universities with need-based aid).
tips: Oxford says overseas undergraduate scholarships are very limited — keep backup funding plans.
avoid: Relying on Reach Oxford as your only funding route.
check: I can explain my financial need and social commitment in a few sentences.

steps.title: Choose your Oxford course and college
steps.why: You must win a place first. The course decides your admissions test and written work.
do: Open the A–Z course list and pick one course (not Medicine).
On the course page, note the required subjects/grades, the admissions test (UAT-UK, LNAT or none) and any written work.
Choose a college or make an open application.
Put all dates into a calendar: test booking deadline, test date, UCAS deadline, written work.
tips: Not all colleges take part in Reach Oxford each year; you may be moved to a participating college if successful.
avoid: Choosing a course without the required A-level subjects.
check: I know my course's test and written work requirements.

steps.title: Book your admissions test (if your course needs one)
steps.why: For 2027 entry Oxford uses UAT-UK tests (ESAT, TMUA, TARA), LNAT for Law and UCAT for Medicine, taken at Pearson VUE centres. Missing the booking deadline ends your application.
do: Read the 2027 admissions tests timeline.
For UAT-UK, register and book before 6pm UK time on 28 September 2026; tests run 12–16 October 2026.
For LNAT, book by 15 September 2026; sit it by 15 October 2026.
Find a Pearson VUE centre near you (e.g. Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt) and practise past papers.
tips: Time yourself on full practice papers in the last three weeks.
avoid: Assuming your school will register you — international applicants usually book themselves.
check: My test is booked (or my course has no test).

steps.title: Plan your English language evidence
steps.why: All Oxford courses require the higher English level, shown by 31 July of the year of your offer.
do: Open the English language requirements page.
Check if your qualifications already meet it (e.g. IB English B at 7 HL, or certain GCSE grades).
If not, plan IELTS Academic (7.5 overall, at least 7.0 in each part) or an accepted equivalent.
Book the test for a date before July 2027.
tips: WAEC English is not listed as accepted evidence — plan for a test.
avoid: Taking the test without practice; component minimums are strict.
check: I have a plan to meet the English level by July 2027.

steps.title: Write your UCAS personal statement
steps.why: Oxford tutors read it for academic interest in your subject, which helps decide shortlisting.
do: Open the Oxford UCAS application guidance.
Use the UCAS format: three sections answering three question prompts, 4,000 characters in total including spaces (Oxford says no changes are expected for 2027 entry).
Spend most of it on your subject: books, problems, projects and what you learned from them.
Mention activities only when they connect to your subject.
Ask a teacher to read it, then finalise.
tips: Oxford tutors care about academic interest; extracurriculars count only if relevant to the course.
check: Most sentences are about my subject and how I think about it.

links.t: Watch: Five top tips for writing your personal statement when applying to Oxford University (University of Oxford)

steps.prompt: Three UCAS question prompts on why you want to study the course, how your learning has prepared you, and relevant experiences outside education.
steps.limit: 4,000 characters in total across three prompted sections

steps.title: Arrange your UCAS school reference
steps.why: UCAS needs a reference (usually from your school) before the application can be sent.
do: Ask your principal, counsellor or A-level teacher to act as referee.
Give them your predicted grades, achievements and personal statement draft.
Agree a date at least a week before 15 October so the school can send the application.
tips: Ask the referee to mention your rank in class and any financial or contextual challenges.
avoid: Leaving the reference to the last two days.
check: My referee has written and attached the reference in UCAS.

steps.title: Submit UCAS by 15 October 2026
steps.why: Reach Oxford applicants must have applied for admission; late UCAS applications to Oxford are not accepted.
do: Complete all UCAS Hub sections and choose Oxford with your course and college code.
Pay the UCAS fee shown at checkout.
Submit (or ask your school to send) before 6pm UK time on 15 October 2026 (the UK is on summer time then, so this is also 6pm in Nigeria).
Save your UCAS Personal ID.
tips: Submit a few days early to avoid card or network problems.
avoid: Confusing UK time with your local time.
check: UCAS shows my Oxford choice as submitted.

links.t: Watch: Oxford undergraduate official guide - How to apply (Undergraduate Study at Oxford)

steps.title: Send written work and prepare for interviews
steps.why: Shortlisted applicants are interviewed online in early to mid-December; this is where tutors judge your thinking.
do: If your course needs written work, send it with the cover form to your college by 10 November.
From late November, check email for a shortlisting decision.
Practise thinking aloud on unfamiliar problems in your subject.
Prepare a quiet room with reliable internet and power backup for the online interview.
tips: Tutors want to see how you reason, not instant correct answers.
avoid: Memorising answers about your personal statement only.
check: My setup is tested and I have practised with a teacher.

steps.title: Complete the Reach Oxford form by 26 January 2027
steps.why: The scholarship has its own application; without it you are not considered.
do: After decisions on 12 January 2027, return to the Reach Oxford page; the form opens in January 2027.
Prepare clear information on family income and why you cannot fund or pursue study in your own country.
Explain your social commitment and plan to return home.
Submit before the 26 January 2027 deadline and save confirmation.
tips: Be precise and honest about finances; give figures in naira with an approximate pound value.
avoid: Missing the January window — it is short.
steps.prompt: Why you need the scholarship, why you cannot study in your own country, and your social commitment (as asked on the form).
steps.limit: As shown on the form — check the current guidance

steps.title: Wait for results and meet conditions
steps.why: Selection happens in April and results come at the end of May 2027.
do: Meet your Oxford offer conditions (exam grades, English level by 31 July).
Watch email for the Reach Oxford result at the end of May 2027.
If successful, follow instructions for college transfer if needed, then apply for your UK Student visa once you have a CAS.
Remember: you must send annual reports and make good progress to keep the award.
tips: Keep backup funding applications active until you have the result.
avoid: Missing the English deadline of 31 July.

faq.q: Can I apply with only WAEC results?
faq.a: No. Oxford lists WASSCE as not accepted; you need A-levels, International A-levels, the IB or another accepted qualification.

faq.q: Is there a separate scholarship form?
faq.a: Yes. After applying via UCAS, complete the Reach Oxford form, which opens in January 2027 and closes 26 January 2027.

faq.q: Can I study Medicine with Reach Oxford?

faq.a: Prepare for 2028 entry: Oxford's UCAS deadline is normally 15 October, with test bookings due weeks earlier. Check UCAS and Oxford for exact 2028 dates.
